About Me & My Skills:
Hello! I am Abdallah, a developer from Jordan. I recently graduated from high school (Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan School) and I am the creator of SANAD-Engine, a custom game engine built from scratch using C++23 and Vulkan. I have strong skills in low-level programming, graphics architecture, and building interactive systems. I am deeply passionate about space exploration and creating immersive digital experiences.

Mission Forge is a 3D educational game in which students design and operate a robotic lunar mission. Players choose a launcher, scientific instruments, communications hardware, and propellant while working within mass, power, and budget limits. They follow the lander they designed from launch through lunar orbit, guide it to a soft landing, and transmit surface science back to Earth.

The game addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by showing how decisions made before launch affect the outcome. A spectrometer can return more science, for example, while increasing mass, power demand, and cost. The mission debrief reports landing accuracy, remaining fuel, and science returned so players can refine their next design. The Earth and Moon visuals use NASA’s Blue Marble and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter imagery.
details:
Mission Forge is a 3D educational game that lets students design and fly a robotic mission to the Moon. In the hangar, players choose a launch vehicle, scientific instruments, solar arrays, communications hardware, and propellant. A flight readiness review checks whether their design meets mass, power, communications, and budget limits before liftoff.

During Guided Launch, players make four decisions about the gravity turn, maximum dynamic pressure (Max Q), booster separation, and payload fairing release. An unsafe command triggers a simulated breakup. The game explains what went wrong, shows how to correct it, and lets players restart at the launch pad with the same design. Hovering over the rocket during ascent reveals a compact portrait of the selected Scout or Heavy launcher.

Players follow the same lander from inside the rocket’s fairing to the lunar surface. They respond to a solar storm, make a course correction, and choose a landing site. After touchdown, they deploy a science probe and transmit their findings to Earth. The mission debrief reports the science returned, landing accuracy, and remaining fuel so players can compare outcomes and refine their next design.

Mission Forge addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by letting students see how engineering decisions affect an entire mission. For example, a spectrometer can increase scientific return while adding mass, drawing more power, and raising costs.

The game runs on SANAD Engine for Windows and uses Lua for mission logic, Vulkan for rendering, and Blender for 3D modeling. The prelaunch briefing draws on NASA’s Design and Develop Science Missions guide. The Earth and Moon visuals use NASA’s Blue Marble imagery and a 4K LROC color mosaic. SANAD Engine and an early Mission Forge prototype existed before the hackathon.
